Confidence Score: 3/5

**[High impact]** Adds NVFP4 quantization support to distributed training\. The PR still needs the two previously reported test-version compatibility issues addressed before merging.

Findings

1.  **Runtime version misses build capability\.** ▶ 2.  **Version probe can crash collection\.** ▶ 3.  **Aligned AllReduce loses overlap\.** ▶

Summary

Adds NVFP4 inputs to the cuBLASMp backend and extends distributed overlap tests. - cuBLASMp GEMMs now accept NVFP4 inputs. - NVFP4 keeps both data layouts for backward GEMMs. Reviews (7) · Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into cublasmp-nvfp4"](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/453fdfb76661226c0d1012228be907e9243b8430) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**NVFP4 tests lack version gate.** If an NVFP4-capable GPU uses a cuBLASMp version older than 0.11.0, this test runs because it checks GPU capability and whether TE was built with cuBLASMp, but not the loaded library version. The new GEMM version check then fails the test instead of skipping it. The layer-test gate at lines 166–170 has the same issue; both paths need a backend-version check.

nodes.body: **Aligned AllReduce loses overlap.** The AllReduce output descriptor gives each rank `n` columns, but this check tests `n / nranks` for 128-column alignment. For example, with `n=128` and eight ranks, it replaces an aligned split algorithm with the default algorithm. Results remain correct, but the operation loses communication overlap and emits a misleading warning. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

nodes.body:
The reference implementation is inconsistent between the high-precision and quantized cases. For high-precision, the reference values are in BF16 and we perform a BF16 GEMM, possibly with split-accumulator. For quantized compute, the reference values are in FP32 and we perform an FP64 GEMM without split-accumulator. See this PR's GEMM logic here: https://github.com/almogsegal/TransformerEngine/blob/9949b9fdd8b6b138a61f142471482c8ad9bc7e22/tests/pytorch/distributed/run_gemm_with_overlap.py#L611-L620

I propose two options:
1. Always keep the reference values in BF16.

```python
    if with_quantized_compute:
        inp_g.copy_(inp_fp8)
        if opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.AG:
            inp_g = te.distributed.gather_along_first_dim(inp_g, tp_group)[0]
        ker_g.copy_(kernel_t_fp8)
        if opts.bulk_overlap and opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.RS:
            bulk_inp.copy_(bulk_inp_fp8)
        elif ub_obj2 is not None:
            ker2_g.copy_(kernel2_t_fp8)

...

        ref_g, *_ = tex.general_gemm(
            ker_g,
            inp_g,
            out_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            use_split_accumulator=ref_use_split_accumulator,
        )
```

2. Always perform the reference GEMM in FP64.

```python
    if with_quantized_compute:
        inp_g = inp_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
        if opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.AG:
            inp_g = te.distributed.gather_along_first_dim(inp_g, tp_group)[0]
        ker_g = kernel_t_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
        if opts.bulk_overlap and opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.RS:
            bulk_inp = bulk_inp_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
        elif ub_obj2 is not None:
            ker2_g = kernel2_t_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
    else:
        inp_g = inp_g.float()
        ker_g = ker_g.float()
        if opts.bulk_overlap and opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.RS:
            bulk_inp = bulk_inp.float()
        elif ub_obj2 is not None:
            ker2_g = ker2_g.float()

...

    ref_g = torch.matmul(inp_g.double(), ker_g.double().t())
```

I think option 1 is nicer since it requires fewer changes to the existing code.


inline_comments.body:
The reference implementation is inconsistent between the high-precision and quantized cases. For high-precision, the reference values are in BF16 and we perform a BF16 GEMM, possibly with split-accumulator. For quantized compute, the reference values are in FP32 and we perform an FP64 GEMM without split-accumulator. See this PR's GEMM logic here: https://github.com/almogsegal/TransformerEngine/blob/9949b9fdd8b6b138a61f142471482c8ad9bc7e22/tests/pytorch/distributed/run_gemm_with_overlap.py#L611-L620

I propose two options:
1. Always keep the reference values in BF16.

```python
    if with_quantized_compute:
        inp_g.copy_(inp_fp8)
        if opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.AG:
            inp_g = te.distributed.gather_along_first_dim(inp_g, tp_group)[0]
        ker_g.copy_(kernel_t_fp8)
        if opts.bulk_overlap and opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.RS:
            bulk_inp.copy_(bulk_inp_fp8)
        elif ub_obj2 is not None:
            ker2_g.copy_(kernel2_t_fp8)

...

        ref_g, *_ = tex.general_gemm(
            ker_g,
            inp_g,
            out_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            use_split_accumulator=ref_use_split_accumulator,
        )
```

2. Always perform the reference GEMM in FP64.

```python
    if with_quantized_compute:
        inp_g = inp_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
        if opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.AG:
            inp_g = te.distributed.gather_along_first_dim(inp_g, tp_group)[0]
        ker_g = kernel_t_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
        if opts.bulk_overlap and opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.RS:
            bulk_inp = bulk_inp_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
        elif ub_obj2 is not None:
            ker2_g = kernel2_t_fp8.dequantize(dtype=torch.float32)
    else:
        inp_g = inp_g.float()
        ker_g = ker_g.float()
        if opts.bulk_overlap and opts.comm_type == tex.CommOverlapType.RS:
            bulk_inp = bulk_inp.float()
        elif ub_obj2 is not None:
            ker2_g = ker2_g.float()

...

    ref_g = torch.matmul(inp_g.double(), ker_g.double().t())
```

I think option 1 is nicer since it requires fewer changes to the existing code.
